name: Louisiana Creole

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Louisiana Creole French (loui1240).
French superstrate/lexifier: vocabulary is primarily of French origin, as French is the language's lexifier (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Creole).
Bambara (Mande) substrate: the largest single group among enslaved Senegambians brought to Louisiana spoke Bambara/Malinke dialects (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Creole).
Wolof substrate, among the Senegambian languages (with Malinke, Sereer, Pulaar) that two-thirds of enslaved people brought to Louisiana spoke (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Creole).
Pulaar (Fula) substrate, among the Senegambian source languages of Louisiana's enslaved population (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Creole).

notes: Skeleton. French-lexifier creole of Louisiana written in a Latin, French-based spelling. Grapheme map follows French conventions adapted to the creole: ou [u], ch [ʃ], j [ʒ], gn [ɲ], the nasal-vowel digraphs an/en [ã], on [ɔ̃], in [ɛ̃], and accented è/é. Orthographic practice varies between writers and etymological French spellings; final silent letters, liaison and any prosody are not reliably recoverable and are left unencoded, so a PER floor is expected. Louisiana Creole stress is largely predictable from French-derived stress patterns and is not separately orthographically marked; left unencoded (documented exemption).
